goal: Iske baad aap samjha sakte hain ke array ka naam uske pehle element ka address hota hai, a[i] aur *(a + i) ko ek hi cheez ki tarah use kar sakte hain, pointer se array mein chal sakte hain, aur bata sakte hain ke array ka naam hilaya kyun nahi ja sakta.
warmup: University ke corridor mein lockers ki ek row ka tasawwur karein, jo ek ke baad ek number kiye hue hain. Agar aap ko pata hai ke locker 0 kahan hai, to aap locker 5 ko 5 lockers aage chal kar dhoond sakte hain. Aap ko har locker ke liye alag naqsha nahi chahiye. Array bhi aise hi kaam karta hai: computer sirf yaad rakhta hai ke pehla box KAHAN hai, aur baqi koi bhi box us se aage boxes ginne se mil jata hai.
definition: Week 4 mein aap ne array ke box tak pahunchne ke liye a[i] use kiya tha. Is lesson ka bada idea: array ka naam (jaise a) uske pehle element ka address hota hai, is liye a ka matlab &a[0] jaisa hi hai. Pointer ek variable hai jo address store karta hai (Week 9). To aap int *p = a; likh sakte hain aur p pehle box par point karega. Kyunke boxes ek saath saath rakhe hain, p + 1 agla box hai, p + 2 us ke baad wala, aur isi tarah. Isi liye a[i] aur *(a + i) bilkul ek hi cheez hain: 'a se shuru karo, i boxes aage jao, andar dekho'.
howItWorks: Memory visual kholein aur Next dabayein. Pehle 4 boxes bante hain jin ke addresses 0x1000, 0x1004, 0x1008, 0x100C hain (4 bytes ke faasle par, kyunke int 4 bytes leta hai). Jab aap int *p = a; likhte hain to pointer p mein 0x1000 store ho jata hai. Computer jama karne mein samajhdar hai: p + 1 sirf 1 byte jama NAHI karta, woh poora ek int jama karta hai, is liye p + 1 hai 0x1004. Aap pointer ko p++ se hila bhi sakte hain aur *p se parh sakte hain. Do shakalein ek hi matlab rakhti hain: a[i] hai *(a + i), aur &a[i] hai a + i (syntax block dekhein). Ab array ke naam aur pointer variable ke darmiyan ahem FARQ. (1) Pointer aam variable hai: aap badal sakte hain ke woh kahan point kare (p++, p = &a[3]). Array ka naam ek fixed address hai, locker 0 ki position ki tarah: usay hilaya nahi ja sakta, is liye a++ aur a = something errors hain. (2) sizeof(a) POORE array ka size deta hai (5 ints = 20 bytes), lekin sizeof(p) sirf ek address ka size deta hai, is liye aap pointer se yeh pata nahi laga sakte ke array mein kitne elements hain. Examples mein hum asli addresses kabhi print nahi karte (woh run ba run badalte hain); hum values print karte hain, p - a jaise farq, aur p == &a[0] jaise comparisons.
